title: Outlook: 1-year and 2-year offline email sync options in new Outlook for Windows
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, existing offline control and product licensing statement are supported. Independent searches found no documented administrator control for the longer sync-window values or published changes to existing values.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans a one-year offline email option in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: In the new Outlook for Windows, users can choose to save 1 year or 2 years of email on their device for offline access.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans a two-year offline email option in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: In the new Outlook for Windows, users can choose to save 1 year or 2 years of email on their device for offline access.

claims.claim: The planned choices extend existing offline settings.
claims.quote: This expands the existing offline settings and allows users to access more email when they are not connected to the internet.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Choosing a longer window saves more email on the device for access without an internet connection.
claims.quote: users can choose to save 1 year or 2 years of email on their device for offline access. This expands the existing offline settings and allows users to access more email when they are not connected to the internet.

Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the one-year and two-year options.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook offline "1 year" "2 years" "Days of email"; "new Outlook" "1-year" "2-year" licensing default storage. Opened release-notes-outlook-new and policy-management; no passage documenting these options.

claims.claim: The cited historical release-note entry is dated May 30, 2025 and identifies version 20250523006.11.
That historical release note says the default offline mail sync window expanded from seven days to 30 days.
claims.quote: The default mail sync window in offline mode has been expanded from seven days to 30 days.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The longer-window capability is user-opt-in: users choose the new values.
claims.quote: users can choose to save 1 year or 2 years of email on their device for offline access

claims.claim: No administrator action to enable these additional choices is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook for Windows" "Days of email to save" administrator policy PowerShell Graph default. Opened policy-management and Set-OwaMailboxPolicy; found the existing offline switch, not an enablement step for the new choices.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No administrator UI setting or API for the number of offline email days is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy OfflineEnabledWin offline sync window days admin policy; "new Outlook for Windows" "Days of email to save" administrator policy PowerShell Graph default. Opened policy-management, EAC policy properties and Set-OwaMailboxPolicy; no window-value control found.

claims.claim: The EAC route to the existing policy's Offline access section is Roles > Outlook web app policies > policy > Details > Access > Manage access > Edit access > Offline access.
claims.quote: go to **Roles** > **Outlook web app policies**. ... **Details** flyout ... **Access**: Select **Manage access**. In the **Edit access** flyout that opens ... **Offline access**

claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell supports Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -Identity <policy name> -OfflineEnabledWin $false to block offline capabilities.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the Outlook on the web mailbox policy that you want to modify. ... $false: Users can't manage offline capabilities in Outlook. No items are saved to the user's device. Previously save items are deleted.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing OfflineEnabledWin switch allows or blocks offline use of new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: The `OfflineEnabledWin` parameter on the **Set-OwaMailboxPolicy** cmdlet allows or blocks the new Outlook for Windows from being used offline.

claims.claim: OfflineEnabledWin controls availability of offline capabilities rather than the number of saved days.
claims.quote: The OfflineEnabledWin parameter specifies whether offline capabilities are available in Outlook ... Valid values are: ... $true: Users can manage offline capabilities in Outlook. ... $false: Users can't manage offline capabilities in Outlook.

claims.claim: Included is the licensing model for this new option within the already licensed Outlook desktop product.
claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft's licensing page says using classic or new Outlook for Windows with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address requires a plan including the desktop Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: The licensing page says Microsoft 365 accounts with a Frontline license cannot be added to new Outlook.
claims.quote:
Can Microsoft 365 accounts with a Frontline license be added to new Outlook?

No.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No license requirement specific to these new sync-window choices is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "1-year" "2-year" licensing default storage; "new Outlook" "offline" "price" "license". Opened licensing-options and release-notes-outlook-new; no option-specific entitlement found.

claims.claim: No price or meter specific to this option is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook offline "1 year" "2 years" default license price storage requirements sync window; "new Outlook" "offline" "price" "license". Opened licensing-options and release-notes-outlook-new; no specific price or meter found.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no license for the option.
claims.quote: The new options are available under Settings > General > Offline > Days of email to save, giving users greater flexibility based on their storage and offline needs.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that introducing these choices changes the default number of saved days.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "1 year" "2 years" offline storage accounts default; "new Outlook for Windows" "Days of email to save" administrator policy PowerShell Graph default. Opened release-notes-outlook-new and Set-OwaMailboxPolicy; no default change tied to these choices found.

claims.claim: No source found says introduction of these options changes existing users' saved-window values.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "1 year" "2 years" offline storage accounts default. Read the roadmap description and opened release-notes-outlook-new and policy-management; no migration or change to existing values found.

claims.claim: Eligibility or account-type exclusions specific to the longer choices are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "1 year" "2 years" offline storage accounts default. Opened licensing-options, policy-management and release-notes-outlook-new; found general product licensing but no eligibility rules specific to these choices.

claims.claim: Storage requirements or mailbox-size limits specific to the longer choices are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook offline "1 year" "2 years" default license price storage requirements sync window; "new Outlook" "1 year" "2 years" offline storage accounts default. Opened release-notes-outlook-new and policy-management; no option-specific requirements found.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no automated action as part of this change.

claims.claim: Microsoft's classic Outlook guidance warns that raising the sync-window value for hundreds or more clients simultaneously could adversely affect network bandwidth.
claims.quote: Applying a higher value to hundreds or more clients at the same time could adversely affect available network bandwidth.

claims.claim: The classic Outlook bulk-resynchronization warning is not documented for these new Outlook choices.
claims.quote: Searched: "new Outlook" "offline" "sync window" "policy"; "new Outlook" "1 year" "2 years" offline storage accounts default. Opened only-subset-items-synchronized and release-notes-outlook-new; the warning concerns classic Outlook SyncWindowSetting, not these choices.
